newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank says won't change money policy.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank says won't change money policy.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Saturday it would not tighten its monetary policy despite a relatively low 1997 consumer price growth target set by the cabinet.

"Because the central bank has to be concerned about both inflation and economic growth, we will not change our current stable-to-loose monetary policy," central bank vice governor Hsu Chia-tung told reporters.

Central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on Friday the cabinet's 1997 consumer price growth target of 3.0 percent was too low and would require the central bank to tighten policy, thus risking a slowdown of Taiwan's economic recovery.
Vice governor Hsu said on Saturday the central bank would maintain its own inflation target of 3.31 percent for 1997 despite the cabinet's insistence on a lower goal.

The bank's decision to maintain current money policy followed its announcement earlier on Saturday that Taiwan's broadest money supply measure, M2, grew a below-target 7.95 percent in December from a year earlier.
Analysts said the December M2 growth, lowest since April, may indicate that Taiwan's ongoing economic recovery was still proceeding at a slow pace.
Taiwan's consumer price growth for the whole 1996 was 3.07 percent.
